concept.logline: A descent through the ocean in which the light goes out colour by colour, yet most of what lives below makes its own.
concept.viewer_change: They can place the light zones, feel what pressure does, and know that the dark deep sea is not dark of light.
concept.central_metaphor: the water column as a descent in which the world loses colour, gains weight and then lights itself

arc.notes: beats use the library stage names loosely: s1 threshold, s2 descent, s3 descent (weight), s4 discovery, s5 return

global_direction.sound_design: one bed per depth zone, darkening and sparse; foley only where something physical happens; 76 bells synchronised to the dots; silence before the reveal and at the end; no whooshes on transitions
global_direction.pacing: slow, 7-13 s per beat, camera always moving during narration

beats.purpose: Start at the bright surface and show light being used up: colour by colour.
beats.viewer_takeaway: The sea is bright only near the surface, and the colours leave in a fixed order.
beats.narration: The sea looks bright from the surface. But sunlight does not travel far. Red light is filtered out first, and blue goes deepest.
beats.visual_concept: A water plate with caustics and light beams; the surface and a boat leave the top of the frame as the camera sinks; a five-band colour strip loses red, orange, yellow and green in turn, and blue is left, glowing.

shots.composition: surface leaving frame top, strip right, gauge left

audio.intent: airy shimmer and bubbles, muffling as it sinks

beats.purpose: Mark the twilight zone and make the dimming felt.
beats.viewer_takeaway: Below 200 m there is rarely any significant light; the twilight zone runs to 1,000 m.
beats.narration: Below two hundred metres, there is rarely any significant light. This is the twilight zone, and it reaches down to one thousand metres.
beats.visual_concept: The camera continues down; light shafts die; a pale jelly drifts up through marine snow; the depth gauge brackets 200 to 1,000 m.

shots.composition: jelly lower-right, zone label lower-left, gauge left

transition_in.motivation: a vertical push reads as the camera continuing downward

beats.purpose: Make pressure felt as weight, not as a fact.
beats.viewer_takeaway: Pressure rises about one atmosphere every ten metres, roughly 1,100 atm at the Challenger Deep.
beats.narration: Going down, the pressure builds. It rises by about one atmosphere for every ten metres. At the bottom of the Challenger Deep, that adds up to roughly eleven hundred atmospheres.
beats.visual_concept: A field of horizontal lines slowly closes as a counter climbs from 1 to 1,090 atm and the gauge runs to 10,900 m; the numeral warms to amber as it climbs.

shots.composition: big numeral centre-left, line field right

audio.intent: rising rumble, creaks as the lines close

assets.reason: exact numbers: deterministic code is the right medium

transition_in.motivation: a slow dissolve: depth as a change of state, not a place

beats.purpose: Turn the surprise into a picture: no sunlight, yet three in four make light.
beats.viewer_takeaway: The deep sea is not empty or dark of life: in this study 76% of observed individuals were bioluminescent.
beats.narration: Below one thousand metres, no sunlight reaches at all. Yet in seventeen years of video off California, about three in four animals seen made their own light.
beats.visual_concept: A hundred dim dots; seventy-six ignite one by one, each with a soft bell; then 76% resolves beside them with its scope.

shots.composition: dot field right, big percentage left

audio.intent: near silence, then 76 bells exactly on the dots

assets.reason: 76 of 100 is a count: draw it exactly

transition_in.motivation: an iris opens like a porthole onto the dark

beats.visual_concept: Everything dims; the dots drift aside and one line of type remains.

audio.intent: bed dissolves; one soft bell; silence at the end

assets.reason: same plate as s4: continuity and no extra generation
